name: Reumah
title: Nahor's Concubine
summary: Reumah was the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother. She is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Genesis 22:24, where she is listed as the mother of four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah. Her descendants formed several ethnic groups in the ancient Middle East.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Nahor's Concubine
keyEvents.description: Reumah is mentioned as a secondary wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, in connection with the listing of Nahor's descendants.

keyEvents.title: Mother of four sons
keyEvents.description: Reumah bore four sons to Nahor: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Ma'akah, who became ancestors of various peoples in the region.

keyEvents.title: Nahor's family tree is revealed to Abraham
keyEvents.description: Abraham learned about his brother Nahor's family, including Reumah's children, after he had passed the test involving the sacrifice of Isaac.

keyEvents.title: Connection to Nahor's primary wife Milcah
keyEvents.description: Reumah is mentioned alongside Milcah, Nahor's primary wife, who bore eight sons, including Bethuel, father of Rebekah.
